gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a measured gain for the Yard Master 2's CineWhite UHD-B fabric. The Hook Up measured that material at 1.27 gain (409 nits against 322.8 nits from a gain-1.0 Stewart StudioTek 100 reference), which is close to Elite's claimed 1.3. Retailers list the same screen at 1.0 or 1.1.
standout_why: Here is what each result ChatGPT got does and does not measure. Wirecutter, the cited page, read via the r.jina.ai reader because nytimes.com and the proxy blocked a direct fetch: it used a colorimeter with Calman, but its only portable-screen figures are a 25% brightness loss on the Zuvmitg 120-inch stand screen and about 10 seconds to set up the Lihong pull-up. It names no number for the Yard Master 2, saying only that it 'can be assembled quickly'. ProjectorVerdict (2026-11-05) says it runs no tests itself and gives no gain figure for the Yard Master 2. iTechGuides (2026-10-26) says its picks 'were not tested together' and reports no figures. RaindropChess (2026-07-14) quotes Elite's 1.3 gain and names no instrument. I could not open Esquire (fetch blocked). Retailers disagree on the Yard Master 2's gain: B&H lists 1.0 and ProjectorScreen.com lists 1.1. None of these pages has an independently measured gain or nit figure for the material ChatGPT made its top pick.
decides: This confirms the top pick rather than changing it. The Yard Master 2's fabric measured about 1.27 gain, while Wirecutter measured a thin budget stand screen (Zuvmitg) losing 25% of the projector's brightness. Wirecutter says the same about the XGIMI portable screen ChatGPT listed as 'best for travel', though without a number. So for picture quality, the tensioned Yard Master 2 is backed by measurements. The Lihong pull-up stays the pick for fast setup on Wirecutter's 10-second time. No named reviewer has published figures for ChatGPT's budget and travel picks (VEVOR, Vamvo, JMGO, XGIMI), so those picks rest on maker claims only.

findings.product: Elite Screens Yard Master 2 (CineWhite UHD-B material)
findings.label: Measured gain of CineWhite UHD-B (The Hook Up)
findings.value: 1.27 gain (409 nits peak white; Elite lists 1.3)
findings.source_title: Best Long Throw Projector Screens (The Hook Up)
findings.note: Page dated 2026-06-25; no author named. Peak white measured with an XGIMI Titan Noir Max projector and compared with a Stewart StudioTek 100 reference (gain 1.0) that read 322.8 nits: 409 / 322.8 = 1.27. The page does not name the meter. The sample was a 100-inch fixed-frame AKIA/Elite screen ($139) in CineWhite UHD-B, the material Elite names for the Yard Master 2. It was not the folding-frame Yard Master 2 itself.
